observation_summary: The compiler throws an 'Array index out of bounds' error when attempting to perform peephole constant folding on an array literal used as an assignment target (e.g., [][1] = 1).
hypothesis: The peephole constant folding pass incorrectly attempts to fold array literals even when they are used as the target of an assignment, leading to an invalid operation on the AST structure.
prediction: Adding a guard to check if the node is an assignment target before proceeding with the folding logic will prevent the invalid operation and resolve the crash.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the addition of an 'if (isAssignmentTarget(n)) { return n; }' check at the beginning of the folding logic, which directly confirms that the missing validation of the node's context was the root cause.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by the absence of a guard condition that checks whether an array literal is being used as an assignment target. The fix introduces this missing check, which is the hallmark of a 'Checking' ODC defect. It is not an 'Algorithm/Method' issue because the folding logic itself is not inherently wrong, just applied in an invalid context.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not a rewrite of the folding algorithm, but rather a guard clause to prevent the algorithm from executing in an invalid context.
